name: view
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::view(Tensor(a) self, SymInt[] size) -> Tensor(a). This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract, including overload selection, keyword arguments, returns, raised errors, aliasing and mutation, and no test may be removed or narrowed to this signature. Semantics derived from the tests: view returns a Tensor sharing self's storage, presenting self's elements under the requested shape; the size overload rewrites metadata only (zero-tolerance/exact value comparison), preserves strides, storage offset and the lazy conjugate/negative bits, returns Tensor(a) aliasing self with _is_view() True, supports tuples, lists and size= keyword forms, accepts -1 inferred extents (exactly one), accepts non-contiguous/offset/stride-0 operands when the target is stride-expressible, writes through to the input, and raises RuntimeError/TypeError/ValueError on numel mismatch, two inferred dims, bare negative extent, non-tensor self/size and unviewable layouts. Other registered overload: aten::view.dtype(Tensor(a) self, ScalarType dtype) -> Tensor(a), reached through the same public entry point flag_gems.view with a torch dtype object, positionally or via dtype=; the tests pass no bare positive int, and the single bare int exercised, -1, must be rejected. It reinterprets the trailing dimension in element units sharing storage without autograd view metadata (_is_view() False, _base None, requires_grad False even for grad-requiring input); for different element sizes it requires dim() >= 1, stride(-1) == 1, shape[-1]*itemsize(self) and storage_offset() divisible by the element-size ratio, and rejects odd trailing dimensions, non-unit last stride, non-divisible storage offsets, rank-0 inputs and lazy conjugate/negative inputs; rank-0 inputs are accepted when the element size is unchanged. Registered schemas (verbatim): "aten::view(Tensor(a) self, SymInt[] size) -> Tensor(a)" and "aten::view.dtype(Tensor(a) self, ScalarType dtype) -> Tensor(a)".
